Title: Using mark_safe
Description: Use of mark_safe() may expose cross-site scripting vulnerabilities and should be reviewed.

Title: Executing Shell Command
Description:
Any Python method that executes shell commands
from within, such as subprocess, os or command modules,
has shell injection attack risk. Such methods include os.system
os.popen, os.popen2, os.popen3, os.popen4, popen2.popen2, popen2.popen3, 
popen2.popen4, popen2.Popen3, popen2.Popen4, commands.getoutput, 
commands.getstatusoutput etc.

Title: Importing subprocess module
Description: Consider possible security implications associated with subprocess modules.

Title: Using ftplib
Description: FTP-related functions are being called. FTP is considered insecure. Use SSH/SFTP/SCP or some other encrypted protocol.

Title: Function With Shell Equals True
Description:
Any Python method that executes shell commands
from within, such as subprocess and execute module,
has shell injection attack risk if 'shell=True' argument
is set.

Title: Using XML
Description: Using various XLM methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Methods should be replaced with their defusedxml equivalents.

Title: Assert Used
Description:
It was discovered that some projects used assert to enforce interface constraints.
However, assert is removed with compiling to optimised byte code. 
This caused various protections to be removed. Consider raising a 
semantically meaningful error or AssertionError instead.

Title: Starting A Process With Partial Path
Description:
If an external process execution in Python code occurs with a Partial
path, it poses security risks from malicious attacks such controlling
contents of PATH variable. Methods like subprocess.Popen, subprocess.call,
os.popen, popen2.Popen3, popen2.Popen4, commands.getoutput, commands.getstatusoutput,
os.execl, os.execle have such risk with partial paths.

Title: Weak Cryptography In SNMP
Description:
Using weak cryptographic algorithms in snmp,
such as v3 using noAuthNoPriv., presents security
risk.

Title: Using eval
Description: Use of possibly insecure function - consider using safer ast.literal_eval.

Title: Missing Timeout In Request Calls
Description:
All request calls should have a timeout. Failure to do so can result
in the process to hang indefinitely.

Title: Using random
Description: Standard pseudo-random generators are not suitable for security/cryptographic purposes. Consider using the secrets module instead: https://docs.python.org/library/secrets.html

Title: Using Pickle
Description: Pickle and modules that wrap it can be unsafe when used to deserialize untrusted data, possible security issue.

Title: Using unverified_context
Description: By default, Python will create a secure, verified ssl context for use in such classes as HTTPSConnection. However, it still allows using an insecure context via the _create_unverified_context that reverts to the previous behavior that does not validate certificates or perform hostname checks.

Title: Hardcoding of Passwords in Function Arguments
Description:
Hardcoding passwords in code increases chances of password guessing.
Passwords, when passed as arguments to functions, can be hardcoded
with argument declarations such as 'pass','password','passwd' etc.

Title: Using Marshal
Description: Deserialization with the marshal module is possibly dangerous.

Title: Using load() Method Of YAML
Description:
The yaml.load() function provides the ability to construct an 
arbitrary Python object, which may be dangerous if you receive a
YAML document from an untrusted source. yaml.safe_load() is safer
alternative.

Title: Importing xml_etree module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package, or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called.

Title: Importing xml_expat module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package, or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called.

Title: Using Mako Templates
Description:
Mako, a Python templating system used in Pylons and Pyramid, has 
no environment wide variable escaping mechanism. Hence, all input variables 
must be carefully escaped or Cross Site Scripting (XSS) attacks may happen.

Title: Insecure Use of Logging.Config.Listen
Description:
logging.config.listen function provides the ability to 
listen for external configuration files on a socket server. 
Because portions of the configuration are passed through eval(), 
use of this function may open its users to a security risk. While 
it only connects to localhost and not any remote machine, there are 
scenarios where untrusted code could be run under the account of the 
process which calls listen().

Title: Using Flask App With Debug Set To TRUE
Description:
Running Flask applications in debug mode results in the Werkzeug 
debugger being enabled. This includes a feature that 
allows arbitrary code execution.

Title: Importing xml_pulldom module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package, or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called.

Title: Exec Used
Description: Python's exec method or keyword is used. Various documents describe why exec is risky to use.

Title: Calling Subprocess Without Shell Equals True
Description:
Spawning a process in Python code using 'subprocess' module,
without 'shell=True' reduces shell injection attack risk
but care should be taken to sanitize input.

Title: Hardcoded Binding to All Interfaces
Description:
Hardcoded binding to all network interfaces, such as '0.0.0.0', can 
potentially open up a service to traffic on unintended interfaces, 
that may not be properly documented or secured.

Title: RawSQL Function In Django Used
Description:
The RawSQL() method of Django framework is vulnerable to SQL injection 
attacks.

Title: Using md5
Description: Use of insecure MD2, MD4, MD5, or SHA1 hash function.

Title: Calling Subprocess With Shell Equals True
Description:
Spawning a process in Python code using 'subprocess' module,
via methods such as 'popen' or 'call', poses shell injection 
attack risks for argument 'shell=True'. Input should be sanitized
appropriately.

Title: Wildcard Injections Through Linux Commands
Description:
Linux commands can be executed through Python methods like 
subprocess.Popen, subprocess.call,os.popen, popen2.Popen3, 
popen2.Popen4, commands.getoutput, commands.getstatusoutput,
os.execl, os.execle etc. Many commands, like chown, chmod, tar,
rsync etc., take wildcard '*' character to implement all files 
and folders and can be used to build partial paths. This poses
security risks such as shell injection attacks.

Title: Pass in Except Block
Description:
Errors in Python raise Exceptions for error logging and handling.
However, the use of 'pass' in the 'except' block of the Exception
can lead to ignoring the issue and raising other vulnerabilities.

Title: Importing pickle module
Description: Consider possible security implications associated with pickle modules.

Title: Importing pyghmi module
Description: An IPMI-related module is being imported. IPMI is considered insecure. Use an encrypted protocol.

Title: Using urllib_urlopen
Description: Audit url open for permitted schemes. Allowing use of ‘file:’’ or custom schemes is often unexpected.

Title: Starting Process With No Shell
Description:
Any Python code starting a process, especially
through modules like os, that do not start a shell
may pose a low risk without penetration testing or knowing
where they are called from. Such processes include 
os.execl, os.execle, os.execlp, os.execlpe, os.execv, os.execve, os.execvp, 
os.execvpe, os.spawnl, os.spawnle, os.spawnlp, os.spawnlpe, os.spawnv, 
os.spawnve, os.spawnvp, os.spawnvpe, os.startfile etc.

Title: Using Weak Cryptographic Key
Description:
Cryptographic algorithms like RSA and DSA can be broken
if key length is less than 1024. Hence length of 2048
is recommended. EC keys less than 160 in length can also be broken
so 224 is recommended.

Title: Importing httpoxy module
Description: XMLRPC is particularly dangerous as it is also concerned with communicating data over a network. Use defusedxml.xmlrpc.monkey_patch() function to monkey-patch xmlrpclib and mitigate remote XML attacks.

Title: Using SSL With No Version Specified
Description:
Python code using SSL/TSL with no version specified may use 
broken versions, such as SSL v2, SSL v3, TLS v1, TLS v1.1, for
maximizing compatibility.

Title: Importing xml_sax module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package, or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called.

Title: Extra Function In Django Used
Description:
The extra() method of Django framework is vulnerable to SQL injection 
attacks.

Title: Importing lxml module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package.

Title: Certificate Validation Is Missing
Description:
Encryption is critical to security and using TLS greatly increases this 
security by guaranteeing identity of communicating parties via trusted
certificates. During HTTPS requests, certificates are automatically 
validated. However, if this validation is explicitly turned off, it 
poses security risk.

Title: Importing pycrypto module
Description: pycrypto library is known to have publicly disclosed buffer overflow vulnerability https://github.com/dlitz/pycrypto/issues/176. It is no longer actively maintained and has been deprecated in favor of pyca/cryptography library.

Title: Shell Injection in Paramiko Functions
Description:
Paramiko is a Python library that works with the SSH2 protocol for
secure connections to remote machines.It is intended to run commands on a 
remote host. These commands are run within a shell on the target and are 
vulnerable to various shell injection attacks through 'exec_command'.

Title: No Host Key Verification In SSH
Description:
Encryption is critical to security and ssh can increases it by guaranteeing
identity of communicating parties. This is done by presenting trusted host
keys during connection initialization. If this host key verification is 
disabled, it presents security risk.

Title: Tarfile Extractall Used Without Any Validation
Description:
Using tarfile.extractall() without any validation from user 
can result in security risks in code.

Title: Harcoding of temporary file/directory
Description:
Hardcoding temporary file or directory paths as strings in code
for any purpose increases vulnerability. Strings containing
'/tmp','/var/tmp' etc. and many others indicate this security risk.

Title: Importing ftplib module
Description: A FTP-related module is being imported. FTP is considered insecure. Use SSH/SFTP/SCP or some other encrypted protocol.

Title: Using mktemp_q
Description: Use of insecure and deprecated function (mktemp).

Title: Using Mark_Safe Method In Django
Description:
The mark_safe() method of Django framework is vulnerable to XSS 
attacks.

Title: Bad Version Of SSL Used
Description:
The following versions of SSL and TLS have vulnerabilities:
SSL v2, SSL v3, TLS v1, TLS v1.1. Using them in code presents
security risks and should be avoided. When using SSLv23, bad versions
of SSL/TLS can be used if the flags are not provided.

Title: Importing xmlrpclib module
Description: XMLRPC is particularly dangerous as it is also concerned with communicating data over a network. Use defusedxml.xmlrpc.monkey_patch() function to monkey-patch xmlrpclib and mitigate remote XML attacks.

Title: MD4, MD5 or SHA1 Insecure Hash Functions
Description:
Weak hasing functions such as MD4, MD5 or SHA1
can be used using the Python cryptographic libraries
like hashlib and crypt. Such weak hashes can be broken
easily, presenting security issues in code.

Title: Using Insecure Version of SNMP
Description:
Using insecure version of snmp like v1, v2c etc. present
security risks in code.

Title: Importing xml_minidom module
Description: Using various methods to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace vulnerable imports with the equivalent defusedxml package, or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called.

Title: Using ciphers and modes
Description: Use of insecure cipher or cipher mode. Replace with a known secure cipher such as AES.

Title: Hardcoding SQL Expressions
Description:
SQL injection attacks involve inserting an SQL query via user input.
SQL injection attacks can occur if SQL expressions are built from user 
input using string building operations. Examples of such operations are:
- 'SELECT %s FROM derp;' % var
- 'SELECT thing FROM ' + tab
- 'SELECT ' + val + ' FROM ' + tab + ...
- 'SELECT {} FROM derp;'.format(var)
- f'SELECT foo FROM bar WHERE id = {product}'
- ''SELECT * FROM foo WHERE id = '[VALUE]' ''.replace('[VALUE]', identifier)
If input is not sanitized, SQL injection attacks can happen through execution
commands like: cursor.execute(“SELECT %s FROM derp;” % var)

Title: Hardcoding of Passwords as Default Function Arguments
Description:
Hardcoding passwords in code increases chances of password guessing.
Passwords, when hardcoded as default arguments using declarations such as 
'pass','password','passwd' etc., can cause security risks.

Title: Setting Bad File Permissions
Description:
Python provides chmod to manipulate POSIX file permissions. This can create
security issues when a file is set to group write or executable or 
if a file is set world write or executable.

Title: Using telnetlib
Description: Telnet-related functions are being called. Telnet is considered insecure. Use SSH or some other encrypted protocol.

Title: Importing telnetlib module
Description: A telnet-related module is being imported. Telnet is considered insecure. Use SSH or some other encrypted protocol.

Title: Hardcoding Password as a String
Description:
Hardcoding passwords in code increases chances of password guessing.
Passwords can be hardcoded as variables, dictionary keys, class attributes 
with variable declarations such as 'pass','password','passwd' etc.

Title: Using SSL With Bad Default Values
Description:
Python methods/functions using default values
corresponding to broke SSL/TLS versions, such as 
SSL v2, SSL v3, TLS v1, TLS v1.1, present vulenerabilities
in code.

Title: Auto Escaping in Jinja2
Description:
Jinja2, a Python HTML templating system, has option to 
autoescape on input. When enabled, Jinja2 will filter input 
strings to escape any HTML content 
submitted via template variables. This results in vulnerability
to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.

Title: Continue in Except Block
Description:
Errors in Python raise Exceptions for error logging and handling.
However, the use of 'continue' in the 'except' block of the Exception
when running statements in a loop can lead to ignoring the issue 
and creating other vulnerabilities.
